task: Has Microsoft's growth become more cash-generative over FY2023–FY2025? Highlight what changed in margins, capex and cash conversion.
context: MSFT annual financial statements, using the latest available revisions; this is a retrospective company review for a US equities desk.
FY2023–FY2025 in USD, with FY2022 revenue as the growth baseline.
Cash conversion means operating cash flow / net income; free cash flow is operating cash flow less cash capex.

outputs.name: msft_fundamentals
outputs.description: One row per requested fiscal year, calculated from the saved annual statements.

schema.name: fiscal_year
schema.description: Microsoft fiscal-year label: FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025; ascending order.

schema.name: period_end
schema.description: Actual fiscal-year period-end date, not filing or retrieval date.

schema.name: revenue
schema.description: Annual reported revenue, in unscaled US dollars.

schema.name: revenue_growth
schema.description: Revenue / prior fiscal-year revenue - 1; FY2022 is needed for FY2023.

schema.name: operating_cash_flow
schema.description: Annual net cash provided by operating activities.

schema.name: capex
schema.description: Capital expenditure expressed as a positive cash outflow; normalize the provider sign once.

schema.name: free_cash_flow
schema.description: Operating cash flow minus positive capital expenditure.

schema.name: free_cash_flow_margin
schema.description: Free cash flow divided by revenue.

schema.name: cash_conversion
schema.description: Operating cash flow divided by net income; null if net income is zero.

outputs.name: analyst_memo
outputs.instructions: Write at most 180 words for the desk. State the main finding, cite the relevant fiscal years and computed figures, and explain growth versus cash conversion. Identify the source and latest-restated snapshot basis. Use no Markdown table and do not repeat every row.
